why: Both moved identical traffic with identical diffs, so the decision rests on system judgment, and A's is deeper and better grounded: three-way labels that revealed the actual bill shape (11 of 15 requests are the quantitative agent, which reframed the whole improvement set), a per-conversation cache key measured at -49%, a provider timeout deliberately placed inside the client's real 60s deadline, per-call latency costs measured through the app, and two candidate levers measured and rejected rather than argued. B has genuinely sharper altitude in places — the fan-out note, the seeding-script embedding-space mismatch, the LlamaIndex model-name validation, and a fallback it actually forced to fire cross-vendor — but its timeout rests on a false premise, its headline saving conflates caching with the model swap, and its two-label split blinds it to where the money actually is.
A_best: Labeling each LLM role separately and then measuring the result: 11 of 15 requests came from the per-document quantitative agent, which is the one fact that makes the cost ranking real rather than assumed, and it honestly lands as a needs-decision when the cheap model triples that loop's latency (5.13s -> 16.49s).
B_best: Forcing an actual fall-through end to end through the app's own client and getting a 200 with provider=anthropic — real verification of the one lever everyone else only cites — alongside the two notes that step above Router entirely: the fan-out sets the bill, and the seeding script embeds in a different space than the query path.
A_worst: The user-facing fallback candidate is gpt-4.1-mini, same vendor as the primary, so it does not cover the OpenAI-side failure that is the main reason to want a fallback, and A admits it never exercised the fall-through against a real 5xx or 429.
B_worst: provider_timeout 90 sits outside LlamaIndex's own 60s client timeout, so it cannot stop a generation the app has already abandoned, and it is justified by the incorrect claim that the chat path has no timeout today; compounding that, the -95% headline compares uncached gpt-4o-mini to cached gpt-6-luna, and prompt_cache_key "$feature" points every conversation at one shared cache pool.
